judged_text: The backfill INSERT writes each raw setting entry verbatim via unescaped string interpolation ('#{h}'), bypassing the EmbeddableHost model's before_validation stripping of scheme/path, its format validation, and parameterized escaping. Setting values the old matcher explicitly accepted (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com', 'https://example.com/1234' per the updated embed_controller_spec) would be stored un-normalized and then never match record_for_host's `lower(host) = 'eviltrout.com'` comparison, so those hosts silently stop allowing embeds even once the backfill runs; a stored value containing a single quote raises a SQL syntax error that aborts the migration.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the backfill does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, which (a) interpolates unescaped user-configured data directly into SQL (a single quote in `h` will break the migration / is unsafe), and (b) inserts the raw setting value without going through `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Since later checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, any migrated rows containing `http://...` or `/path` would not match `uri.host` and embeds would be incorrectly rejected after migration.
